html:
The princely state of Mysore was the smaller kingdom the British gave back to the Wadiyar family after they killed Tipu Sultan in 1799. On the 1815 map it is a British ally in southern Karnataka.

The boy king Krishnaraja Wadiyar III was put on the throne at five, with the able minister Purnaiah ruling for him, under a subsidiary alliance with the British. After a peasant revolt in 1831 the British took over the government directly and only handed it back in 1881.

From then on Mysore became known as one of India's best run states. Its dewans, among them the engineer M. Visvesvaraya, built dams, railways, power lines and schools. The Indian Institute of Science opened in Bangalore in 1909. Mysore joined India in 1947 and was absorbed into the Indian state of the same name, later Karnataka. For the earlier kingdom, see Mysore.
